rationale: The AddVoter receipt answered the question in the affirmative on both halves: the added server appears as a Voter rather than a staging server, and on a single-voter cluster that immediately removes the cluster's ability to commit, to elect, and to undo the change through the same API, while the identical change on a three-voter cluster is harmless. This submission records that account with the documented bootstrap workflow it interacts with, promotes the two knowledge entries the account rests on, and keeps the out-of-band recovery path and the stale-documentation reading visible as counterevidence rather than letting the finding stand unqualified.

knowledge.statement: The AddVoter configuration change installs the requested server with Suffrage Voter in one step: nextConfiguration's AddVoter branch builds the new Server with Suffrage Voter, the resulting configuration is appended as a single LogConfiguration (or the deprecated remove-peer entry below protocol version 2), and the leader applies it to the commitment and to replication immediately after dispatching it. Nothing in the captured path creates a Staging server or defers promotion, despite the AddVoter comment that describes the server as added for staging and promoted by the leader once it is ready.
knowledge.conditions: Protocol version 2 or above for the ID-based API; the cluster has a leader able to commit the configuration entry; the requested server may be absent from the cluster entirely (a fresh ID and address).

knowledge.statement: When the configuration change makes the voter quorum exceed the number of living voters, the cluster loses progress and cannot repair itself in band: the leader's lease check finds contact with fewer voters than the quorum, it steps down, no election can complete because the quorum still requires the unreachable server, applies are answered with ErrNotLeader, and RemoveServer for that server is answered with ErrNotLeader so the configuration still lists it. For one added server this happens exactly when the cluster had a single voter; with two or more living voters, adding a voter leaves the quorum satisfiable and the cluster keeps working.
knowledge.conditions: The added server is not running and no transport can reach it; the pre-change cluster was healthy; captured in-memory timers (heartbeat, election and lease all 50ms in this probe).

interpretations.rationale: Retained execution (check 1e88d22c83c34a0a8ceebe331c699fa2, exit 0, tests_passed, 8 parsed events, 0 parse errors). All three declared comparisons hold and are complete. The added server appears with suffrage Voter in both cases (indices 1 and 5), which is the documented staging behaviour absent. On the single-voter cluster (index 1: two voters, one living, quorum 2) comparison 0 holds on result index 2: the apply came back as 'node is not the leader', the node was a Candidate, and the cluster had no leader at all. Comparison 2 holds on result index 3: RemoveServer for the same server also came back as 'node is not the leader' and the configuration still listed two voters, so the change cannot be undone through the API once the leader is gone. The control comparison holds on result index 6: on the three-voter cluster the same operation left the leader in place with a successful apply, and its removal succeeded on index 7, which is what makes the single-voter outcome a consequence of the quorum relation rather than of AddVoter being broken in general. Read with the sources, the account is: the change is a full membership change from the moment it commits, the quorum moves with it, and when the quorum exceeds the living voters the cluster has no leader, no commit and no in-band way back - which the library's own recovery contract reserves for the out-of-band RecoverCluster operation. The interaction that makes this reachable in documented use is that the same comment block that recommends bootstrapping a single server and then adding the other servers with AddVoter is matched by an AddVoter comment that promises the new server is staged and promoted once it is ready; an operator who follows both literally adds servers that are not running yet, and on a single-voter cluster that is exactly the stranding case.
counterevidence: The staging description may simply be stale text: Staging is deprecated in this snapshot and AddNonvoter is the documented replacement for adding a not-yet-voting server, so the intended reading could be that the comment should be corrected rather than the behaviour. That reading does not remove the behavioural half of the account - an operator who follows the comment is still stranded - but it moves the defect from the implementation to the contract it publishes.
Adding a voter that is not running is a membership mistake in Raft terms; the harm here is that the API's own description licenses that workflow by promising a staging step that does not exist.

Recovery is not impossible out of band: RecoverCluster exists precisely for a configuration that cannot be restored, with the documented warning that it implicitly commits the log. So the correct statement is that there is no in-band repair, not that the cluster is unrecoverable.

The consequence needs the quorum relation; for one added server it is specific to a single-voter cluster, and the three-voter control in the same run shows the operation is harmless when the living voters still meet the quorum.
limitations: Two shapes were probed (one living voter and three living voters, one added server each); the general condition is the quorum exceeding the living voters, which the probe brackets rather than enumerates.
The added server is never started, so the promotion path the documentation describes cannot be exercised - there is no such path in the captured code to observe.

The probe runs one process with the in-memory transport, so what an operator would see in a real deployment (a client timing out rather than an ErrNotLeader answer) is inferred from the API's documented error semantics rather than observed.
The claim is about this snapshot's code and its published comments; whether the project considers the comment authoritative is for its maintainers.
